content:
In the sentence "The apple does not fit into the box because it is too big," the pronoun "it" refers to the apple.

Here's the explanation:

The sentence is discussing the inability of an apple to fit into a box because of the apple's size. The subject of the sentence is "The apple," which is the thing that does not fit into the box.

The pronoun "it" is used as a reference to the same object, the apple. When the sentence states "it is too big," the "it" is clearly referring back to the apple mentioned earlier in the sentence.

In other words, the pronoun "it" is used to avoid repeating the word "apple" again in the second part of the sentence. It acts as a replacement for the noun "apple" to make the sentence more concise and avoid redundancy.

So, in this context, "it" unambiguously refers to the apple that was mentioned previously in the sentence.
